Start with the seat, not the candidate. 2026 Democratic vote share versus the district or state's 2024 presidential share. Each dot is one
qualified contest; the diagonal marks equal shares. The diagonal is a descriptive equal-share reference, not an expected generic candidate, election forecast, national-wave adjustment or causal candidate effect. House geography uses the 2026 congressional map. All 470 contests, including the 37 held comparisons, remain in the complete candidate queries.

charts.alt:
Donor ideology gives a selected-sample answer. 2026 House association with a 0.5-point more conservative historical donor score. These scores describe
funding coalitions, not campaign platforms. Every row is a separately fitted observational association. Exact FEC/state/party matches with consistent names qualify. All name discrepancies are excluded here, including four aliases corroborated in a separate identity review. The nonincumbent group is below the 30-person publication gate; its diagnostic estimate and interval are retained in the CSV, not drawn as supported evidence. Models use known incumbency for both parties. No inference extends to all challengers, and the intervals are not multiple-testing-adjusted.

charts.alt:
The baseline changes the donor-ideology answer. 2026 House: a 0.5-point more conservative donor score. The lower two rows use exactly the same
candidates, isolating the benchmark change. The full-sample to restricted-sample change mixes attrition and specification, whereas the lower two rows isolate presidential benchmark choice on identical IDs. The 2020 benchmark is allowed only on independently qualified election maps. This sensitivity argues against treating a single positive coefficient as a universal moderation premium or Split Ticket WAR.

charts.alt:
Same candidates, different ideology signals. 2026 House: the same 100 Democratic incumbents in 30 states. Separate models versus jointly adjusting
for both measures, with the same lean controls. An audit-added, exploratory comparison, not a prespecified confirmation. The common sample contains only verified Democratic incumbents with both scores; it is not representative of all nominees. All four models use identical candidate IDs, lean/lean-squared and available Republican-incumbency controls. Donor ideology describes historical funding coalitions; Nokken-Poole measures recorded congressional votes. Their different scales and opposing associations prohibit a single moderate/progressive ranking. Intervals are pointwise, without multiplicity adjustment.

charts.alt:
What the congressional voting record shows. House: ideology uses prior-Congress votes; 2026 party defection uses votes cast before Election Day. The
two measures have different increments. 2026 ideology is the Congress-specific Nokken-Poole first dimension from 2023-2024 votes, not DW-NOMINATE or current campaign positions. The 2026 defection rate uses qualifying recorded votes from January 2025 through November 2, 2026; older years use prior-completed-Congress records. Changing cohorts and timing prevent a formal trend interpretation. Separate increments are not a ranking of the measures. See CSV for exact sample sizes and Holm values.

charts.alt:
Incumbency comparisons across six elections. Democratic incumbents versus nonincumbents, controlling for constituency lean and Republican incumbency.
2026 is the primary election. Separate annual chamber-specific lean/lean-squared regressions; the cross-year points are not a paired-candidate or formal trend test. Presidential election years use same-year presidential benchmarks; midterms use lagged benchmarks. Senate estimates frequently have limited support. Unknown incumbency is not coded as nonincumbency. These are associations, not causal incumbency effects.

charts.alt:
Caucus membership is a thin test of moderation. Blue Dog minus Progressive Caucus structural residuals. Hollow points are diagnostic: at least one group
falls short of the support gates. Blue Dog/CPC groups are distinct from Blue Dog PAC/CPC PAC endorsements, New Democrats, DSA and Justice Democrats. A 2026 roster of 10 Blue Dogs leaves eight eligible nominees in this model; this does not reconcile the external chart's group of 12. Small membership cohorts, changing benchmark vintages and wide uncertainty do not establish that a moderation premium shrank.

charts.alt:
New biographies reach far beyond incumbents. Share of named 2026 Democratic nominees with a source record. A missing record does not mean that a
candidate lacks a trait or position. The denominator is 454 named nominees, not 470 contests or just winners. 183 incumbents, 249 nonincumbents and 22 nominees with unknown incumbency sum to that denominator. The new corpus supplies pre-election biography records for 147 nonincumbents, versus eight with the older CampaignView historical biographies; the datasets have different years and definitions. No machine-extracted biography has been promoted into a verified trait or model.
